name: Many-Worlds Derivative Transport
definition: A derivative propagation method that treats potential surfaces along a ray as mutually exclusive events, ensuring they do not interact via shadowing or scattering, unlike exponential volume rendering which treats them as independent Poisson processes.
summary: Many-Worlds Derivative Transport computes analytical radiance derivatives for volume rendering by treating surface interactions as mutually exclusive events, unlike Exponential Volume Rendering which allows multiple scattering.
